lead: A keepsake journal for nine-year-olds to fill in, look back on and keep. This year’s theme: strength, curiosity and everyday life.
for: For a nineth birthday present that means a bit more
For children who like to write, draw and think things through
For parents who want this year remembered in their child’s own words

problem.h: This year will go faster than you think
p: Nine is a curious, in-between year. They’re asking bigger questions, finding out what they’re good at and working out friendships for themselves.
Their favourite things change every few months, and the photos and school reports don’t show what it actually felt like to be them.

approach.h: Let them write their own record of the year
p: The Year of Being 9 gives them a private place to write and draw about themselves: what they’re good at, who matters to them, what they love doing, and what they hope for.
Some days they’ll have lots to say, and other days just a little. The journal tells them both are perfectly fine.

offer.h: A whole year of being nine
offer.p: Gentle prompts in calm, simple pages, made to fill in at their own pace.
features: Strengths, what makes them special, and a day that felt like them.
Words for big feelings, what helps, and the people and friends who care about them.
Hobbies, favourite books and films, three wishes, and a note for future me.

decision.h: Paperback or hardcover, it’s your choice
decision.price_note: paperback, at the time of writing
points: The paperback is lighter and a little cheaper.
The hardcover is sturdier, good for a gift or a keepsake meant to last.
Both have the same pages, printed and delivered by Amazon.

faq: Is it right for my nine-year-old?
It’s written for children who are nine, or turning nine. If they’re between ages, choose the year they’re about to start, as they’ll fill it in over the coming months.
Will they need help filling it in?
Most children this age can use it on their own, with help spelling now and then. Many pages can be drawn rather than written.
The pages are the same. Hardcover is sturdier and lasts better on a shelf, and paperback is lighter and a little cheaper.
Is it a good birthday present?
Yes. It’s a thoughtful present for a nineth birthday, and lovely to give alongside a set of pens.
What if they start partway through the year?
That’s fine. Nothing is dated, so they can start any time and fill it in at their own pace.

close.h: Keep being nine in their words
close.p: One journal now, and a shelf of them as they grow.
